scope: Targeted primary-source follow-up for seven catalog gaps; claim-scoped research, not whole-route verification.

claims.topic: Official English-language Korean immigration material describes F-2-7 as a points-based resident status, and an older official government university guidance PDF specifies certain D-2/D-10 graduate applicants with Korean employment and at least 80/120 points. It is not a current comprehensive route handbook and cannot establish present general eligibility or current score schedule.
claims.retrieval: Official Korea Immigration Service indexed PDF, dated circa 2023; route-specific official lead retrieved, current operative rule unconfirmed.

resolvedFields: Route exists as points-based F-2 resident category; limited official evidence describes one graduate/employment branch and historic 80/120 threshold.
unresolvedFields: Current comprehensive route eligibility, exclusions, points table, income/tax criteria, duration, family, renewal and availability.

attempts.outcome: Official government PDF states graduate/employment branch and >=80/120 points, but old and category-limited.
Official F-2 overview lists points-system foreign talent but directs readers to HiKorea for detailed requirements; no current F-2-7 detail.
Portal queried; route-specific current handbook not surfaced.

items.recommendation: Keep availability unclear and do not encode score threshold as current general gate. Obtain current HiKorea 체류민원 자격별 안내 / F-2-7 point table or written Immigration Contact Center confirmation before a new guarded batch.

claims.topic: Portugal's AIMA states national third-country subsistence means are referenced to minimum wage and lists evidence types, including pensions/passive investment income; this supports the route's native means-of-subsistence concept but not a bespoke D7 amount or consular checklist. AIMA source states 2025 minimum wage €870.
claims.retrieval: Official AIMA page retrieved; page explicitly gives 2025 reference amount, not 2026.

claims.topic: Official Portuguese legislation requires residence visa applicants living from movable/immovable assets, intellectual property or financial investments to document existence/amount and availability of such income in Portugal for at least 12 months.
claims.retrieval: Officially hosted Diário da República legal text, retrieved; dated 2007 with later amendments referenced by AIMA.

financialRequirements.amount: Reference amount tied to minimum monthly wage; AIMA page gives €870 for 2025 only
financialRequirements.period: monthly benchmark; route proof period at least 12 months for passive-income category in regulation
financialRequirements.scope: statutory means of subsistence / funds evidence, not fee or total cost

resolvedFields: Native subsistence benchmark framework and evidence basis for passive income; Portugal's broad residence-visa intake exists.
unresolvedFields: Current 2026 benchmark amount; precise D7 consular procedure/checklist and any post-specific interpretations; availability for a specific applicant; renewal and residence-credit details.

attempts.outcome: Retrieved current official page; amount is explicitly 2025 (€870).
Retrieved official regulation; passive-income proof and 12-month period supported.
Current gov.pt residence-visa service found for independent activity/entrepreneur, not D7/passive-income-specific.

items.recommendation: Route availability can be upgraded to open at broad service level, while D7-specific amount remains partial. Keep amount null unless current 2026 wage instrument and responsible consular post checklist are obtained.

claims.topic: ICP describes 10-year Golden Residency for real-estate investors, AED 2 million total property value, full ownership (including specified approved-bank financing/off-plan conditions), and insurance; ICP entry-permit service lists AED 2m ownership proof and AED 300 fees, distinct from capital threshold.
claims.retrieval: ICP official current page directly retrieved.

claims.topic: UAE government portal's category table says real-estate investor Golden Visa is 5 years (and AED 2m); conflicts with ICP's issuing-authority 10-year page.
claims.retrieval: Official government portal page directly retrieved; updated 24 Mar 2026.

financialRequirements.scope: qualifying property value, not fee or liquid-funds requirement

financialRequirements.period: per ICP entry permit service listed fees: application 100, issuance 100, smart services 100
financialRequirements.scope: procedural service charges, not full Golden Residency application fee schedule

resolvedFields: AED 2m real estate threshold and key ownership/insurance conditions; ICP currently describes 10 years and provides the responsible service entry point.
unresolvedFields: Duration discrepancy: ICP says 10 years while u.ae says 5 years for real-estate category. Final issued permit validity by emirate/service not established; full fees not established.

attempts.outcome: Retrieved: 10-year property Golden Residency; AED 2m conditions.
Retrieved ICP service: fully owned property and AED 2m letter; service fees total AED 300, but service card says entry permit to complete Golden Residency.
Retrieved government portal: 5-year property visa; direct conflict persists.

items.recommendation: Keep conflict explicitly disputed; do not select a single generic duration. Preserve AED 2m as supported threshold and route availability as open for the ICP Golden Residency product, with a duration caveat pending ICP case/service-level confirmation.

claims.topic: Montenegro government currently describes temporary residence based on ownership/use of domestic real estate, generally issued for one year. Its current Law on Foreigners page published May 14, 2026 provides enacted legal text; the older Article 56 establishes the property ground without a value floor. Government 2025 communications describe EUR 200,000 as a draft/proposed change, not operative law. The May 2026 law file is located but its text was not retrieved in this pass to verify amendments/transitional provisions.
claims.retrieval: Official government service information retrieved.

claims.topic: Government announced a EUR 200,000 threshold in a draft amendment; this is legislative proposal evidence, not proof of enacted rule.
claims.retrieval: Official government draft/announcement directly retrieved.

resolvedFields: A property-based temporary residence ground exists under published official guidance; standard validity one year. EUR 200,000 is demonstrably described as proposed/draft in 2025, not established by that announcement as current enacted minimum.
unresolvedFields: Whether the new Law on Foreigners published 14 May 2026 enacted an amended minimum, commencement date, grandfathering/deadline and current application implementation.

attempts.outcome: Retrieved: real-estate ground and one-year permit.
Retrieved: EUR 200,000 proposal described as draft.
Current May 2026 law document landing page found; source PDF not opened/parsed, so enactment details not concluded.
Official older English law text confirms property residence article but is not current enactment.

items.recommendation: Change interpretation only in a new batch after reading the May 2026 enacted law and commencement article. Current public ministry guidance alone supports the route but cannot disprove a recent amendment.

claims.topic: Panama Migration Service current official decree index lists Executive Decree 16 of 31 Aug 2026, modifying Decree 416 (Friendly Nations), as amended by Decrees 197/2021 and 226/2021, to add Ecuador to the eligible-country list. Current 2026 agency statistics record approvals under Países Amigos, showing current use of the category. Exact full eligibility alternatives/documents and complete current nationality list were not read from the decree text.
claims.retrieval: Official Migration Service decree index directly retrieved.

resolvedFields: Friendly Nations is an enacted/current and actively used category as of 2026; latest listed amendment adds Ecuador.
unresolvedFields: Complete current nationality list and whether any excluded nationality restrictions apply; qualifying economic ties/jobs/investment alternatives; required amounts, dependents, renewal/permanent status and total charges.

attempts.outcome: Retrieved current decree list, including 2026 amendment adding Ecuador and references to 2021 modifications.
Official stats list 619 Países Amigos residence approvals through March 2026; confirms active category use, not detailed eligibility.
Decree download link for Decree 16 available in index, exact text not parsed in this pass.

items.recommendation: Availability may be marked open. Keep nationality and legal conditions incomplete until reading consolidated Decree 416/197 or Decree 16 plus 197 and 226 in official gazette, and current Migration Service checklist. Do not rely on legacy country lists.

claims.topic: Vanuatu Citizenship Office publishes the Citizenship Act consolidated edition and DSP Regulations Order 33 of 2019. The Act authorizes citizenship by DSP and requires regulation-set fees and decision within three months; 2019 regulation sets payment staging (25% before consideration, 75% before certificate), nonrefundable initial portion, criminal-conviction restriction, restricted-country conditions, and certificate within 90 days after approval. An official Citizenship Office directive states 2019 government minimum contributions/retail prices: single USD 80,000 minimum contribution / USD 130,000 retail; married couple USD 100,000 / 150,000; married plus 1 child USD 115,000 / 165,000; married plus 2 children USD 130,000 / 180,000. Directive is dated 2020 and fee schedule currency is USD.
claims.retrieval: Official Citizenship Office regulation PDF retrieved.

claims.topic: Official DSP fee directive states minimum contribution and selling price by family size; it is an official enforcement directive but not a newly dated 2026 schedule.
claims.retrieval: Official office PDF dated 30 Apr 2020 retrieved.

financialRequirements.scope: minimum contribution, single applicant; official 2020 directive; differs from retail price
government minimum retail price, single applicant, per 2020 directive; not a fee-only figure
government minimum retail price, married couple

resolvedFields: DSP is a statutory citizenship route, not residence; official 2019 rules and official fee directive support its legal basis, payment sequencing, some restrictions and historically published minimum amounts.
unresolvedFields: Whether 2019/2020 USD amounts remain current in 2026, complete due-diligence/agent/admin charges, extra-dependent calculation and present country restrictions/list, current application availability and policy updates.

attempts.outcome: Retrieved Citizenship Office index of Act, amendments and DSP 2019 regulation.
Retrieved official rules: staged payment, no refund of first portion, processing constraints and restrictions.
Retrieved official directive dated 30 Apr 2020 with USD contribution and minimum retail price tiers.
Official page says forms page under construction and applications should obtain authentic forms from Citizenship Office.

items.recommendation: Retain DSP route but label fee evidence historical (2020 directive) and do not claim current total program price. Seek written 2026 Citizenship Office confirmation and current restricted-country schedule before financial fields or intake state are upgraded.

claims.topic: State Department's Aug 31 2026 DV notice contains a decisive within-page contradiction: top update says December 2025 pause ended Aug 28 following court order; immediately afterward says effective immediately all DV issuances are paused. FAQ says none issued, interviews continue. This follow-up retrieved the same official notice and does not find a superseding official DV-specific notice. Thus actual operational issuance status cannot be resolved from the official notice; current legal/operational posture remains disputed, while program deadlines are year-specific.
claims.retrieval: Official State Department notice directly retrieved; internal contradiction confirmed.

claims.topic: State Department says DV-2027 application period is Oct 1 2026 to Sep 30 2027 for selected applicants, while the DV-2027 entry registration dates are to be announced; this does not establish a currently open entry window.
claims.retrieval: Official State Department notice directly retrieved.

resolvedFields: No unqualified open/closed conclusion from the contradictory official DV issuance notice; registration and visa issuance are separate, year-specific states. DV-2027 entry dates were not stated in the located notice.
unresolvedFields: Whether DV issuances are actually paused after the notice's conflicting sentences; any later court order/agency clarification after page publication; current DV-2027 registration window.

attempts.outcome: Retrieved; contradiction remains on the single official notice.
Retrieved; says DV-2027 entry date announcement forthcoming, selected applicants' program period Oct 1 2026-Sep 30 2027.
Retrieved, concerns 75-nationality IV pause ending by court order; does not directly resolve separate DV-specific pause.

items.recommendation: Keep issuance status disputed/source conflict and no primary availability claim. Do not equate court order ending prior pause with end of subsequent newly announced pause. Recheck State Department DV notice and court docket for a post-notice clarification before any new batch.

claims.topic: Current consolidated Montenegro Law on Foreigners, Article 56: property-based temporary residence requires land-register/ownership evidence plus tax valuation issued by the local administration; the transfer-tax valuation base may not be below EUR 150,000. Owner or co-owner may qualify. EU/EEA/Swiss nationals and their family are exempt from providing this valuation evidence. This supersedes treating EUR 200,000 as a confirmed enacted threshold; the 2025 government announcement explicitly described EUR 200,000 as a draft proposal.
claims.retrieval: Consolidated legal text retrieved from secondary Montenegro legal database; not official host.

claims.topic: Official Gazette registry records the 2026 amendments published 9 Jan 2026 effective 17 Jan 2026. A later law published 19 Oct 2026 takes effect 27 Oct 2026, after this research check date, so it is not applied to the 25 Oct current-law answer.
claims.retrieval: Official Gazette registry retrieved directly; May 2026 ministry law PDF download timed out in web reader.

financialRequirements.scope: Minimum tax base of valuation evidence under Article 56, not free-standing property purchase price; EU/EEA/Swiss applicants and family exempt from that proof.

resolvedFields: Property route exists; owner or co-owner; ownership/folio and local tax authority valuation; current consolidated Article 56 valuation tax base floor EUR 150,000; one-year permit per official gov.me service page.
unresolvedFields: Primary Gazette article text not independently parsed because the official May 2026 PDF timed out; retrieved exact Article 56 from secondary consolidation. Property-route work rights and presence/renewal conditions not specifically reviewed.

attempts.outcome: Official May 2026 Law on Foreigners landing page retrieved; attached PDF URL timed out.
Official Gazette says Jan 2026 amendments effective 17 Jan 2026.
Oct 2026 amendment has future effective date 27 Oct 2026; excluded from 25 Oct rule snapshot.
Consolidated Article 56 retrieved with EUR 150k valuation threshold.

followupResearch.recommendation: Availability can be marked open and EUR 200k draft threshold replaced with EUR 150k valuation-tax-base evidence, subject to a primary-text citation limitation. Keep the valuation evidence distinct from an investment or assessed market-value obligation.

claims.topic: The official gov.pt service (updated 22 May 2026) explicitly provides a residence-visa service for retirees and people living on their own income. It lists passport, photos, travel insurance, Portuguese and origin/residence criminal records, accommodation and subsistence evidence; retirees provide pension amount and own-income applicants show income sufficient for subsistence. It directs applicants to the competent consular post. This is the official service corresponding to the commonly named D7 route.
claims.retrieval: Official gov.pt page retrieved, updated 22 May 2026.

claims.topic: Official DGERT lists 2026 RMMG as EUR 920 effective Jan 1, 2026 under Decree-Law 139/2025. Portaria 1563/2007 Article 2 uses RMMG net of social-security contributions; first adult 100%, each additional adult 50%, each child under 18 or dependent adult child 30%. Article 5(6) requires passive income/pension subsistence means for at least 12 months with evidence of amount and availability in Portugal. This is a generic statutory means framework, not a D7-specific consular income floor.
claims.retrieval: Official DGERT and Diário da República legal text retrieved.

financialRequirements.scope: Generic statutory means index only; family weights 100/50/30%, net-of-social-security wording, and passive income evidence at least 12 months. Not a D7-specific income floor or fee.

resolvedFields: Official route existence/intake as retiree or own-income residence visa; general checklist; native RMMG year updated; family-scale formula and 12-month passive-income evidence.
unresolvedFields: No single D7-specific income cutoff in official service; competent consular post may define document handling/sufficiency. Do not compute exact family totals from gross EUR 920 because the legal formula references the amount net of social-security contributions.

attempts.outcome: Retrieved current route-specific service and checklist.
Retrieved 2026 amount EUR 920 effective Jan 1.
Retrieved legal family formula and 12-month passive-income requirement.

followupResearch.recommendation: Mark broad route available. Use EUR 920 as the dated statutory index with formula details; do not label it a D7-specific floor. Keep amount matching/calculation claim partial and post-specific instructions unresolved.

claims.topic: Official Gazette Decree 16/2026 amends Article 2 of Decree 416 (as modified by 226): eligible applicants are only nationals of the amended country list; Ecuador was added effective 1 Sep 2026. The decree says Ecuadorians follow Decree 226 procedure, costs, guarantee deposits and two-year provisional residence stage; it retains the rest of 226 requirements, stages and fees. It also says economic/professional/investment activity must be evidenced; residence does not waive work permit or permit regulated professions.
claims.retrieval: Official Gazette searchable text directly retrieved; full amended nationality list spans pp.17-18.

claims.topic: Official Migration Service indexed checklist lists three economic ties: local employment with company/work-permit documents, property value B/.200,000 (local bank financing allowed), or unencumbered B/.200,000 fixed deposit maintained for three years. Current PDF URL now returns 404, so this detailed checklist was obtained through the official-domain search index rather than live PDF body.
claims.retrieval: Search-index text from official SNM domain; direct fetch returned 404.

financialRequirements.scope: Property alternative eligibility tie; local bank financing allowed.

resolvedFields: Open active permanent-residence category; exact nationality gate and current 51-country list including Ecuador; two-year provisional stage; three current documented qualification branches and separation from work authorization.
unresolvedFields: Original 2021 Decree 226 is scan-based and detailed current checklist link currently 404; checklist is indexed but not directly fetched. No generic processing time identified.

attempts.outcome: Official Gazette text confirms country list, Ecuador addition, two-year provisional and 226 terms retained.
Official checklist text found indexed; URL currently 404 on direct open.

followupResearch.recommendation: May mark broad route open with nationality gate and distinct employment/property/deposit branches; preserve the checklist retrieval limit and no processing estimate.

claims.topic: HiKorea, the official immigration portal, lists the newest integrated manuals dated 2026-10-19, including visa application and stay-qualification manuals. The notice says it updates manuals when guidelines change but uploads may lag; for the latest specific instruction it directs applicants to call 1345 or book/visit immigration. The HWP attachment text did not parse in web reader, so no current points details are taken from it.
claims.retrieval: Official HiKorea notice directly retrieved; manual attachment date/name visible; HWP contents inaccessible in this web reader.

claims.topic: Official 2026 government immigration policy plan names the F-2-7 talent-track initiative and labels the implementation task completed in 2023. This shows historical program action status, not that the underlying F-2-7 status is abolished; current practical rules should be taken from latest HiKorea manual, which exists as of 19 Oct 2026.
claims.retrieval: Official current 2026 policy plan PDF retrieved; relevant section located.

resolvedFields: There is current official route-specific manual infrastructure as of 19 Oct 2026 and F-2-7 remains in the current immigration taxonomy. The historic 80/120 point claim relates to a narrow graduate/employment branch and cannot be generalised.
unresolvedFields: Current eligible applicant groups, score table/threshold, income/tax, exclusions, duration, work/family and availability are not extracted from HWP attachment and must remain unencoded.

attempts.outcome: Official notice retrieved; Oct 19 2026 HWP manual attachments listed, but reader did not expose download contents.
Official 2026 plan confirms policy-track task concluded in 2023, not cancellation of visa category.

followupResearch.recommendation: Upgrade evidence to current manual availability but keep all substantive criteria unresolved until HWP attachment is extracted or 1345 confirms. Do not cite historical 80-point graduate threshold as universal current gate.

Separately it lists FIU diligence fee USD5,000; VUV5,000 application fee excluding Form D, paid at lodgment; citizenship fee paid only after approval. The page is current on the 2026 office website but has no schedule-effective date and tells applicants to contact the office for correct figures.
